_comment: THE ONE PLACE THE DOMAIN IS WRITTEN. base-services renders the Caddyfile from this file (platform/tools/edge/render.py) and bring-up.sh feeds the result to the cluster as a ConfigMap — so a route added here is a route the edge serves, and a Caddyfile edited by hand is a file that gets overwritten. Values are validated before they are interpolated; a hostname that does not parse stops the install rather than becoming a site block.
_domain: Set by bring-up.sh from DOMAIN at install time — the installer asks once and every layer below reads the same answer. The value here is the local default, for a box with no DNS.
_aliases: Set by bring-up.sh alongside domain — affiliates.<DOMAIN> and admin.<DOMAIN>. Same site block, same routes, same cert (one SAN list): the console image is still what answers, and it is the console's own router that reads the hostname and decides which tree to mount (see main.tsx). An alias buys a distinct address, not a distinct upstream.
_routes: Longest prefix wins and the renderer sorts, so listing order cannot shadow a route. The last entry is the catch-all: everything that is not an API call is the console image, which carries the landing page at / and the screens under /app and does its own SPA fallback.

routes._p: The customer's own page, opened from a WhatsApp link. It is the only path here a person reaches without a token, and it belongs to portal rather than to the console.
